title: Explainability and fairness
hook: Explaining single decisions, checking groups, and keeping a human path for appeals.
inPlainWords: A model can be accurate and still unfair, or impossible to explain. Explainability asks "why this decision?". Fairness asks "does it treat groups of people differently in ways we cannot justify?"

useCase.title: Decide who is offered "buy now, pay later"
useCase.story: ShopEase offers buy-now-pay-later to some customers. A model scores who to approve. Declined customers ask why, regulators may ask for evidence, and the team worries the model treats some groups worse.

approaches.name: Inherently readable models
approaches.what: Use a model whose logic can be read directly, like a small tree or a linear model.
approaches.greatWhen: Stakes are high and the loss in accuracy is small.
approaches.example: Approve if on-time payments are high and the balance is low.

approaches.name: Global explanations
approaches.what: Show which factors matter most across all decisions.
approaches.greatWhen: Checking the model makes sense overall.
approaches.avoidWhen: You need the reason for one person's decision.
approaches.example: Payment history matters most, then income stability.

approaches.name: Explanations for one decision
approaches.what: Show the top reasons behind a single decision.
approaches.avoidWhen: Treating the reasons as proof of cause.
approaches.example: Declined mainly because of two late payments last quarter.

approaches.name: What-if hints (counterfactuals)
approaches.what: Show the smallest change that would flip the decision.
approaches.greatWhen: Telling people what they could do.
approaches.example: Approved if the current balance were $200 lower.

approaches.name: Fairness checks by group
approaches.what: Compare approval rates and error rates across groups.
approaches.example: Compare false declines by age band and region.

approaches.name: Fixes for gaps
approaches.what: Reduce unfair signals, rebalance data, adjust thresholds, or add human review.
approaches.greatWhen: A gap is found and cannot be justified.
approaches.avoidWhen: Deleting one column while close stand-ins, like postcode, remain.
approaches.example: Review borderline declines with a person.

challenge.question: Customers are declined and ask why, and someone asks whether some groups are treated worse. What is the strongest approach?

options.text: Explain each decision, test error rates by group, review the gaps, and keep a human appeal path
options.why: It answers the customer, the auditor and the team.
A model can be 92% accurate and still treat one group badly.

options.text: Delete the sensitive column and call it fair
options.why: Close stand-ins, like postcode, can carry the same signal.
Transparent, but that is not the same as explaining a decision or checking fairness.

bestCase.title: Explain each decision, test by group, and keep a human appeal
bestCase.example: A declined customer sees the two main reasons and a "what would change this" hint. A monthly report compares false declines across groups. A gap found for one region is traced to a data problem and fixed, and borderline cases go to a person.

worstCase.title: A black box judged only on overall accuracy
worstCase.example: The model is 92% accurate overall but wrongly declines one group twice as often. Nobody can explain individual decisions, complaints pile up, and the company cannot show it ever checked.

steps.label: Top reasons for this decision
steps.goes: Two late payments last quarter are the main reason.
steps.goesWrong: No reasons are recorded. The team says "the model decided".

steps.label: What-if hint
steps.goes: A lower current balance would flip the result.

steps.label: Fairness report by group
steps.goes: False declines are compared across groups every month.

steps.label: Investigate gaps
steps.goes: Any gap is traced to its cause and fixed.

steps.label: Human appeal path
steps.goes: A person can review and override the decision.

takeaway: Accuracy is not enough for decisions about people. Explain each one, test across groups, and keep a human path.
